app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — `<%- end if %>` is a Ruby syntax error (`end if ;`); the primary view never renders. Confirmed by compiling the template. Controller specs don't render_views, so nothing catches it.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — SSRF: open-uri follows redirects with no re-validation; TopicRetriever only checks the *initial* host, so an allowlisted host can 302 to 169.254.169.254 or 127.0.0.1:6379 and the response body is imported into a public topic (exfiltration).

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `import_remote` fetches before any scheme check (the `^https?` guard is in `import`, which runs after); a caller like disqus.thor:147 passing untrusted XML links reaches Kernel#open with `|command` (subprocess exec) or `file:///etc/passwd`.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — no read_timeout, size cap, or content-type check; an allowlisted host can stream unbounded data into a Sidekiq worker (DoS).

app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — stored XSS: `"<a href='#{url}'>"` interpolates the URL into a single-quoted attribute unescaped, stored as raw_html and emitted with `raw`. `http://allowed.host/x'onmouseover='...` breaks out.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` passed to import with no sanitizer at all; unescapeHTML actively converts `<script>` back into `<script>`, stored verbatim in posts.cooked.

app/models/post.rb:131 — `return raw if cook_method == raw_html` makes `cooked` a verbatim copy of untrusted remote HTML, bypassing post_analyzer.cook AND the Plugin::Filter extension point. Every existing template rendering post.cooked becomes an XSS sink.
app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 — `<%= raw post.cooked %>` is the sink for the above.

app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — raw `Referer` header interpolated unescaped into a JS string literal used as postMessage targetOrigin; a referer of `http://allowed.host/x'+alert(1)+'` passes ensure_embeddable (host-only check) and executes in the forum origin. Also: a full URL with path is an invalid targetOrigin, so resize silently never delivers.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — the only gate on the endpoint is a client-controlled Referer header; it gates both the `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` relaxation and the server-side fetch trigger.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — unauthenticated job enqueue with no rate limit and no host validation at the controller; the per-URL redis throttle keys on the full URL, so `?embed_url=http://allowed.host/?n=1..N` defeats it → unbounded Sidekiq/Redis growth, unbounded auto-created topics, traffic amplification at the allowlisted host.
lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 — host-only check: scheme, port, userinfo unconstrained. `ftp://allowed.host/` and `http://allowed.host:6379/` both pass. No blank-host guard.
lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — `skip_validations` bypass is now available to every PostRevisor caller, not just TopicEmbed.
app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:18 — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, not an origin equality check; `http://d` passes. `e.source` never verified.

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — UNIQUE(embed_url) on a raw unnormalized URL is the wrong business key: http/https, trailing slash, www., case, and utm_* params each create a distinct row and a duplicate topic for the same article. The URL comes from whatever the host page set in discourseEmbedUrl — this is the normal case.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:15-30 — TOCTOU: `where(...).first` then `create!`. The unique index makes the loser raise unrescued RecordNotUnique after a topic was already created. Reachable in normal operation since TopicRetriever invokes PollFeed inline.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:13,16 — content_sha1 is computed AFTER appending the I18n `imported_from` footer, making the change-detection digest locale- and translation-dependent: alternating PollFeed/import_remote locales causes a spurious revision every time, and editing the locale string rewrites every imported post.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 — `revise!`'s return value is ignored but `update_column(:content_sha1, ...)` runs unconditionally; a failed revision permanently marks the embed up-to-date and the stale post is never re-synced.
db/migrate/20131217174004:4-5 — topic_id and post_id stored side by side with no FKs, no indexes, no dependent: cleanup; post.topic_id already determines topic_id (redundant, can go stale).

db/migrate/20131217174004:11 — orphan case is not benign: topic_id_for_embed returns a dead topic_id (500 in the iframe), and because embed_url is UNIQUE, re-import takes the else branch where `embed.post` is nil → `PostRevisor.new(nil)` raises. db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `add_column ... default: 1, null: false` on `posts` forces a full table rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on PG of this era; a single-step rolling deploy is an outage.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:40-43 — a per-request regular job synchronously runs an entire scheduled hourly job (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`); one cache-miss embed hit downloads and imports the whole feed, N concurrent misses trigger N full polls. Guard conditions duplicated at the caller.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:21-33 — the redis SETNX is a rate-limit marker, not a lock: set before work begins, expires on a fixed 60s timer regardless of outcome. `no_throttle` for staff removes it entirely, so two concurrent staff requests both run perform_retrieve on the same URL.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:44-53 — layering violation: an ActiveRecord model performs outbound HTTP + HTML extraction with no timeout/size cap/redirect policy.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:64-71 — absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs: `//cdn.example.com/x.png` → `http://blog.com/cdn.example.com/x.png` (verified by executing the expression). app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `contents << ...` mutates the caller's string in place; raises on a frozen string, double-appends on reuse.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:24-31 — the embed allowlist is a single scalar SiteSetting: one host only, no www./apex pair, no staging host. Supporting the obvious next requirement forces a settings migration.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 — TopicView.new on a topic_id from topic_embeds with no existence/visibility precheck; a deleted topic yields an unhandled exception inside a third-party iframe.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:1 — `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` misuses the Rails autoload API for a rubygem; lazy-require strategy for the two new `require: false` gems is scattered across three call sites with no owner.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `open(url).read` but this file never requires 'open-uri' (only poll_feed.rb does); the EmbedController→RetrieveTopic→import_remote path gets Kernel#open and raises Errno::ENOENT.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which calls `open(url).read` after requiring only `ruby-readability`. Unlike `Jobs::PollFeed`, this code path does not `require 'open-uri'`. In the EmbedController → RetrieveTopic → TopicRetriever → import_remote flow, `open` will be Ruby’s default `Kernel#open` unless `open-uri` has been loaded elsewhere, so it may try to open a local file named like `http://...` and raise `Errno::ENOENT`. The diff itself provides no guarantee that `open-uri` is required before this path runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43 — spec expects `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`, but the controller enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`; unmet mocha expectation → spec fails as written.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb#best`, when no topic_id is found it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. The controller does not instantiate or call `TopicRetriever` anywhere. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` (the test around line ~43) sets `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, which will not be satisfied by the controller code path, so the spec will fail as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:50 — `TopicView.expects(:new)` returns nil, so `@topic_view` is nil in best.html.erb; the shared `after` block asserts success → cannot pass.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the expectation `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` does not specify a return value, so Mocha would return `nil` by default. However, in typical RSpec controller specs (and nothing in this diff enables `render_views`), templates like `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` are not rendered/evaluated, so `@topic_view` being `nil` would not cause a failure. The controller action itself also does not dereference `@topic_view` before responding. Therefore the claimed “cannot pass because best.html.erb uses @topic_view” is not a verifiable problem from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — SSRF: open-uri follows redirects with no re-validation; TopicRetriever only checks the *initial* host, so an allowlisted host can 302 to 169.254.169.254 or 127.0.0.1:6379 and the response body is imported into a public topic (exfiltration).

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only validates the host of the original `@embed_url` (`URI(@embed_url).host` vs `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`). But the actual HTTP fetch happens in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` (open-uri). open-uri will follow redirects by default, and there is no subsequent validation of the final redirected-to URL/host. Therefore an allowlisted host could 302/301 redirect to an internal address (e.g., 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1, or RFC1918), and the response body would be read and then imported into a topic via `TopicEmbed.import(...)` (ultimately stored as post raw/html). This is a concrete SSRF/exfiltration risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `import_remote` fetches before any scheme check (the `^https?` guard is in `import`, which runs after); a caller like disqus.thor:147 passing untrusted XML links reaches Kernel#open with `|command` (subprocess exec) or `file:///etc/passwd`.

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` on the caller-supplied `url` before any validation. The only `^https?` guard is in `import`, which runs *after* the fetch. Because `open` is Kernel#open (and may be extended by open-uri elsewhere), passing a string like `|cmd` can invoke a subprocess, and non-HTTP schemes like `file:///etc/passwd` can be opened as local files. This is reachable from the new code path in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`) where `t[:link]` comes from parsed input, so the diff introduces a real security issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — no read_timeout, size cap, or content-type check; an allowlisted host can stream unbounded data into a Sidekiq worker (DoS).

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import_remote the code does `open(url).read` and passes the full body into Readability::Document. There is no explicit limit on bytes read, no validation of response Content-Type, and no streaming/early abort; it will attempt to read the entire response into memory in a Sidekiq job (`RetrieveTopic` / `TopicRetriever`). Even though `TopicRetriever` restricts the host to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, an allowlisted host can still respond with an arbitrarily large body (or non-HTML) and cause excessive memory/CPU usage in the worker (DoS risk). The lack of explicit timeouts/limits is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — stored XSS: `"<a href='#{url}'>"` interpolates the URL into a single-quoted attribute unescaped, stored as raw_html and emitted with `raw`. `http://allowed.host/x'onmouseover='...` breaks out.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In TopicEmbed.import, it appends HTML to `contents` using `"#{url}"` with no escaping. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which still allows single quotes in the remainder of the URL (e.g. `http://allowed.host/x'onmouseover='...`). Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged, and `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, the injected attribute-breakout would be stored and executed when displayed.

In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, feed item content is set to `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then passed to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates the post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)`.

In `Post#cook`, the new logic `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline, so the HTML is effectively stored/served as-is (and `embed/best.html.erb` renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`). `CGI.unescapeHTML` can indeed turn `<script>` into `<script>`, making it possible for malicious/compromised feed content to become executable HTML/JS in rendered posts. No sanitizer is applied in this path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:131 — `return raw if cook_method == raw_html` makes `cooked` a verbatim copy of untrusted remote HTML, bypassing post_analyzer.cook AND the Plugin::Filter extension point. Every existing template rendering post.cooked becomes an XSS sink.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` with a `:raw_html` option and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses `post_analyzer.cook(*args)` (the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline) and also bypasses `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. The diff then introduces code paths that set `cook_method: :raw_html` for remotely sourced content (`TopicEmbed.import` via RSS `i.content` and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` via `open(url).read` + readability). That remote HTML is not run through Discourse’s normal sanitizer here, and at least one new view renders it explicitly unescaped (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb` uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>`). Therefore this change does introduce a verifiable XSS risk from untrusted remote HTML and also skips the plugin extension point, as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 — `<%= raw post.cooked %>` is the sink for the above.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a new `cook_method` of `:raw_html` in `Post#cook` that returns `raw` directly, bypassing Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` and `PollFeed` can create/update posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using feed/readability content that is not sanitized in this diff (RSS path is just `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` plus URL absolutizing). In `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, `<%= raw post.cooked %>` will therefore render untrusted HTML directly into the embed page, creating a verifiable XSS sink on the Discourse origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — raw `Referer` header interpolated unescaped into a JS string literal used as postMessage targetOrigin; a referer of `http://allowed.host/x'+alert(1)+'` passes ensure_embeddable (host-only check) and executes in the forum origin. Also: a full URL with path is an invalid targetOrigin, so resize silently never delivers.
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly notes that using a full referrer URL (including path) as postMessage targetOrigin is invalid and causes the resize message to be dropped, which is the same underlying issue as the golden comment (targetOrigin must be scheme+host+port/origin).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — the only gate on the endpoint is a client-controlled Referer header; it gates both the `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` relaxation and the server-side fetch trigger.
matched_golden_ids: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the endpoint’s protection relies on a client-controlled Referer header and that this gate controls the relaxation to `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL`, which aligns with the golden issue about disabling clickjacking protection and bypassable referer validation. It doesn’t explicitly mention the nil-referer empty-string fallback masking failures, but it identifies the core vulnerability (referer-based bypass + ALLOWALL).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — unauthenticated job enqueue with no rate limit and no host validation at the controller; the per-URL redis throttle keys on the full URL, so `?embed_url=http://allowed.host/?n=1..N` defeats it → unbounded Sidekiq/Redis growth, unbounded auto-created topics, traffic amplification at the allowlisted host.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, any request that passes ensure_embeddable enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, embed_url: ...) when no TopicEmbed exists, with no authentication or rate limiting at the controller level. ensure_embeddable validates only the Referer host against SiteSetting.embeddable_host, but does not validate params[:embed_url] before enqueueing (host validation happens later inside TopicRetriever#invalid_host? in the background job, so invalid embed_url values can still create jobs). TopicRetriever’s throttle key is "retrieved:#{@embed_url}", i.e., the full URL string; varying the query string (e.g., ?n=1..N) yields distinct Redis keys and bypasses the 60-second throttle, allowing an attacker to enqueue unbounded Sidekiq jobs and force repeated remote fetches (open(url)) to the allowlisted host, and potentially auto-create many topics for distinct URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 — host-only check: scheme, port, userinfo unconstrained. `ftp://allowed.host/` and `http://allowed.host:6379/` both pass. No blank-host guard.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb `invalid_host?` only compares `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` to `URI(@embed_url).host`. That means any URL whose *host* matches will be treated as valid regardless of scheme or port (e.g. `ftp://allowed.host/...` or `http://allowed.host:6379/...`), and `fetch_http` will then call `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which does `open(url).read`, potentially fetching non-HTTP(S) resources or unexpected services on nonstandard ports. However, the finding’s “No blank-host guard” part is not accurate: if `embeddable_host` is nil/blank, the comparison will fail and the URL will be treated as invalid (and specs cover the nil case).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — `skip_validations` bypass is now available to every PostRevisor caller, not just TopicEmbed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor to honor an internal option (`@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`), which allows callers to intentionally bypass validations. While it’s true that *any* code path that calls `revise!` could now pass `skip_validations: true`, the diff does not show any untrusted/param-driven caller gaining access to this option, nor any incorrect existing caller unintentionally passing it. The only new usage in the diff is `TopicEmbed` explicitly using it for imports, which appears intentional. So the finding describes a broadening of an internal API, but not a verifiable defect/security issue introduced by the diff on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:18 — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, not an origin equality check; `http://d` passes. `e.source` never verified.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that using `indexOf` for origin validation is unsafe because it performs a substring check rather than strict origin equality, allowing malicious origins/domains to bypass the check (e.g., attacker-controlled domains containing the trusted URL).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — UNIQUE(embed_url) on a raw unnormalized URL is the wrong business key: http/https, trailing slash, www., case, and utm_* params each create a distinct row and a duplicate topic for the same article. The URL comes from whatever the host page set in discourseEmbedUrl — this is the normal case.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `topic_embeds.embed_url` the sole unique key (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`) and all lookups are exact-string matches (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url)` and `topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)`), but there is no normalization/canonicalization of URLs anywhere in `TopicEmbed.import`, `import_remote`, `TopicRetriever`, or `EmbedController` before storing/looking up. Therefore the same underlying article can produce multiple different `embed_url` strings (http vs https, trailing slash, different query params like utm_*, etc.), which will not hit the existing row and will create duplicate topics/embeds. This is a real correctness/business-key defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15-30 — TOCTOU: `where(...).first` then `create!`. The unique index makes the loser raise unrescued RecordNotUnique after a topic was already created. Reachable in normal operation since TopicRetriever invokes PollFeed inline.

adjudication.rationale:
In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a non-atomic check-then-act:

- It looks up `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`.
- If blank, it enters a transaction and later calls `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)`.

There is a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). If two workers import the same `url` concurrently, both can observe `embed.blank?` and both attempt `create!`; the loser will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`, and nothing in `import` rescues it.

This is reachable: `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` can call `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline, and multiple `TopicRetriever` jobs for different `@embed_url`s can run concurrently (throttle is per `@embed_url`, not per feed polling), causing concurrent `PollFeed` executions against the same feed and thus races on the same item URLs.

The transaction will likely roll back the losing attempt (so it may not leave persistent duplicates), but the unhandled exception is still a real correctness/availability defect (job/request failure) introduced by this pattern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13,16 — content_sha1 is computed AFTER appending the I18n `imported_from` footer, making the change-detection digest locale- and translation-dependent: alternating PollFeed/import_remote locales causes a spurious revision every time, and editing the locale string rewrites every imported post.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends an I18n-translated footer to `contents` (`contents << ... I18n.t('embed.imported_from', ...)`) and only then computes `content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)`. That means the stored digest depends on the current translation string/locale, not purely the upstream article content. If the translation text or active locale differs between imports/polls, the SHA1 will change even when the source content hasn’t, triggering the `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` branch and causing unnecessary `PostRevisor` updates and rewriting of the stored post body/footer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 — `revise!`'s return value is ignored but `update_column(:content_sha1, ...)` runs unconditionally; a failed revision permanently marks the embed up-to-date and the stale post is never re-synced.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, when an existing embed’s content changes (content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1), it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then immediately executes `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` without checking whether the revision actually succeeded. The diff shows `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` (it explicitly does `return false if not should_revise?`) and `update_post` now uses `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` (non-bang), so a failed save/revision could fail without raising. In that case, the embed would be marked up-to-date anyway, preventing future re-sync attempts because subsequent imports will see matching SHA1s and skip revising.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004:4-5 — topic_id and post_id stored side by side with no FKs, no indexes, no dependent: cleanup; post.topic_id already determines topic_id (redundant, can go stale).

adjudication.rationale: The migration does create `topic_embeds` with both `topic_id` and `post_id` and only adds a unique index on `embed_url`, so it’s true there are no DB-level FKs and no indexes on `topic_id`/`post_id`. However, the finding frames this as a clear defect (redundant/stale data) which is not verifiably a bug from the diff: the code explicitly uses `topic_id` for fast lookup (`topic_id_for_embed` plucks `:topic_id` by `embed_url`) without joining through `post`, suggesting the redundancy is intentional. Whether `topic_id` can “go stale” depends on post/topic reassignment behavior not shown in the diff, making that part speculative. Missing FKs/dependent cleanup is also an architectural preference and not a demonstrated correctness/security break here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004:11 — orphan case is not benign: topic_id_for_embed returns a dead topic_id (500 in the iframe), and because embed_url is UNIQUE, re-import takes the else branch where `embed.post` is nil → `PostRevisor.new(nil)` raises. A deleted embedded topic can never be recreated for that URL.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff adds `TopicEmbed` with `embed_url` uniquely indexed and lookup/branching logic that assumes the associated `topic`/`post` always exist. `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` (`pluck(:topic_id).first`) does not verify the topic exists, so a stale `topic_embeds` row can yield a non-existent `topic_id`, and `EmbedController#best` will call `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)`, which would raise if the topic is missing. Separately, `TopicEmbed.import` takes the `else` path whenever a `topic_embeds` row exists for the URL, sets `post = embed.post`, and unconditionally constructs `PostRevisor.new(post)` when content changes; if the referenced post was deleted (no FK/cascade is added in the migration), `embed.post` can be nil and this will error instead of recreating. The unique index prevents creating a second row for the same URL, so the code has no recovery path for this orphaned state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `add_column ... default: 1, null: false` on `posts` forces a full table rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on PG of this era; a single-step rolling deploy is an outage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new migration `AddCookMethodToPosts` that runs `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions common in the Rails 4 / 2013 era, adding a column with a non-null default typically rewrites the entire table and holds an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration, blocking reads/writes to `posts`. Given `posts` is usually a large/hot table, this is a concrete deploy-time outage risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:40-43 — a per-request regular job synchronously runs an entire scheduled hourly job (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`); one cache-miss embed hit downloads and imports the whole feed, N concurrent misses trigger N full polls. Guard conditions duplicated at the caller.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb `perform_retrieve` runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before falling back to `fetch_http`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does a network fetch (`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and iterates/imports all feed items, so a single embed cache miss can trigger a full feed poll/import. Because `TopicRetriever` is invoked per embed URL miss (controller enqueues `:retrieve_topic`, which calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`), multiple concurrent misses can each execute the full poll. The guard conditions are also partially duplicated: `perform_retrieve` only checks `feed_polling_enabled?`, while `PollFeed#execute` re-checks `feed_polling_enabled?`, `feed_polling_url.present?`, and `embed_by_username.present?`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:21-33 — the redis SETNX is a rate-limit marker, not a lock: set before work begins, expires on a fixed 60s timer regardless of outcome. `no_throttle` for staff removes it entirely, so two concurrent staff requests both run perform_retrieve on the same URL.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, `perform_retrieve` is skipped only if `retrieved_recently?` returns true. In `retrieved_recently?`, when `@opts[:no_throttle]` is set (used for staff via `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` in the job), it immediately returns `false` and does not set the Redis `setnx` key at all. That means two concurrent staff-triggered calls for the same `@embed_url` will both proceed into `perform_retrieve`. `perform_retrieve` only does a non-atomic `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` check before doing work, so both can race past the existence check and attempt import concurrently (the unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` may cause one to error after creating a topic/post). Also, for non-staff, the Redis key is set before work begins and expires after 60s regardless of success/failure, matching the finding’s “marker not lock” description.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:44-53 — layering violation: an ActiveRecord model performs outbound HTTP + HTML extraction with no timeout/size cap/redirect policy.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/models/topic_embed.rb` method `self.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (open-uri) to fetch remote content directly from within an ActiveRecord model, then parses/extracts HTML via `Readability::Document`. The diff shows no explicit timeout, max size/streaming limit, or redirect policy, so this can block workers/requests and download arbitrarily large/redirected content. This is a concrete, verifiable concern introduced by the diff (not just style).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64-71 — absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs: `//cdn.example.com/x.png` → `http://blog.com/cdn.example.com/x.png` (verified by executing the expression). Document-relative refs (`foo.html`, `../x.png`) are never absolutized despite the docstring claiming "any relative URLs".

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, any `href`/`src` that starts with `/` is rewritten as `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`. For protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.png`, `start_with?('/')` is true and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` turns it into `cdn.example.com/x.png`, producing `http://blog.com/cdn.example.com/x.png`, which is incorrect corruption of the original URL. Also, despite the comment claiming it converts “any relative URLs”, the implementation only handles root-relative paths (`/path`) and ignores other relative forms like `foo.html` or `../x.png`, so the behavior does not match the docstring.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `contents << ...` mutates the caller's string in place; raises on a frozen string, double-appends on reuse.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the line `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends to the `contents` argument in place. This is directly verifiable in the diff and can cause incorrect behavior if the caller reuses the same String instance (it will accumulate multiple "Imported from" footers across calls) and will raise `FrozenError` if a frozen string is passed (e.g., caller-provided frozen content). This is a real correctness defect because mutating method arguments is observable and not documented/expected here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:24-31 — the embed allowlist is a single scalar SiteSetting: one host only, no www./apex pair, no staging host. Supporting the obvious next requirement forces a settings migration.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces a single string setting `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and enforces an exact host match in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` (`URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`). That does mean only one host value is accepted at a time, but the proposed finding is about anticipated future requirements (multiple hosts, www/apex pairs, staging) and the need for a settings migration later. That’s not a verifiable defect/bug/security issue in the diff itself—it's a product/design limitation and speculative maintenance concern rather than a concrete problem the change introduces.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 — TopicView.new on a topic_id from topic_embeds with no existence/visibility precheck; a deleted topic yields an unhandled exception inside a third-party iframe.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, a topic_id is fetched via TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) and immediately used in TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5}) with no check that the Topic still exists or is accessible. The diff adds topic_embeds with only an index on embed_url and no foreign key constraints or dependent-destroy behavior, so it’s plausible for a TopicEmbed row to remain after a topic/post is deleted. In that case topic_id_for_embed would still return an id, and TopicView.new would likely raise (e.g., RecordNotFound) resulting in an unhandled 500 in the embed iframe.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:1 — `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` misuses the Rails autoload API for a rubygem; lazy-require strategy for the two new `require: false` gems is scattered across three call sites with no owner.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` in `TopicEmbed`, and uses `require 'simple-rss'` / `require 'ruby-readability'` inside methods. This is not a verifiable bug or correctness/security defect: `require_dependency` will still load the gem via `require` and typically won’t break runtime behavior, and “scattered lazy-require strategy with no owner” is a design preference/maintainability critique rather than a concrete defect introduced by the change. Nothing in the diff demonstrates malfunction caused by these requires.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20-22 — `feed_key` is dead code (verified by grep): it implies a conditional-GET/Last-Modified layer that was never wired up, so every poll re-downloads and re-imports the whole feed.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` is defined (lines ~20-22) but never referenced anywhere in the diff: `execute` calls `poll_feed`, and `poll_feed` directly does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` without using `feed_key` or any stored state. So `feed_key` is dead/unused code, and there is no implemented conditional-GET/Last-Modified (or any caching) layer—each scheduled run will re-fetch the feed over HTTP and iterate all items again. The “re-imports the whole feed” part is slightly overstated since `TopicEmbed.import` dedupes by `embed_url` and `content_sha1`, but the job still re-downloads and re-processes the entire feed every time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — `i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 feeds carrying <description>; `nil.scrub` raises. No per-item rescue, so one bad item aborts every remaining item; with `retry: false` the hourly poll is silently dropped.
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags that `i.content` can be nil (e.g., RSS 2.0 feeds that only provide `<description>`), causing `nil.scrub` to raise—same core bug as the golden comment. It also notes broader failure impact, but the underlying issue (missing content field and need for fallback such as description) matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open()/SimpleRSS.parse unguarded: 404/timeout/malformed feed raises with no logging.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is executed with no `begin/rescue`. Both `open(...)` (via `open-uri`) and `SimpleRSS.parse` can raise exceptions on HTTP errors (e.g., 404), timeouts, connection failures, or malformed feeds. Since the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, an exception will abort the run and it won’t be retried; there’s also no explicit logging or fallback behavior in this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:57 — `URI(url)` can still raise InvalidURIError for URLs passing the `^https?` regex (spaces, brackets); unrescued.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the only validation on `url` is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which only checks the prefix. `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` then calls `uri = URI(url)` with no rescue. Ruby's `URI()` can raise `URI::InvalidURIError` for URLs that still match the regex (e.g., containing spaces, unescaped brackets, other invalid characters). This exception would propagate and break the import path (`PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents) ...)`), so the finding identifies a real correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — no rescue for OpenURI::HTTPError/timeouts/Readability/Nokogiri; `doc.title` may be nil → topic with nil title.
app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — no terminal failure state: on fetch failure the loading view reloads every 30s forever with no error shown to the reader.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil it enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` and renders `embed/loading`. The `loading.html.erb` template unconditionally executes `document.location.reload()` after 30s, with no retry limit and no branch for a failed/never-succeeding retrieval. Since the job can fail silently (e.g., network error in `open(url)` / feed parsing) or never create a `TopicEmbed`, the iframe will keep reloading indefinitely without surfacing an error state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` also caches the loading branch, while loading.html.erb reloads after 30s — the reload can be served the cached loading page instead of the ready topic.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed unconditionally after either rendering the topic view or rendering `loading`. That means the `loading` response will also be sent with a 60s cache lifetime. Since `loading.html.erb` triggers `document.location.reload()` after 30s (which may reuse cached content depending on browser/cache headers), a client can plausibly get the cached loading page again instead of fetching the now-ready topic within that 1 minute window. This is a concrete behavior implied directly by the diff (cache header applied to both branches + 30s reload).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:49 / poll_feed.rb:26 — if embed_by_username names a nonexistent user, both return silently with no logging; combined with the loading view the embed spins forever.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, it does `user = User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and then `return if user.blank?`, with no error/logging. In `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, it does the same and returns if blank. Meanwhile `EmbedController#best` renders the `loading` view whenever no `TopicEmbed` exists, and that view reloads every 30s; each request enqueues `:retrieve_topic` again. If `embed_by_username` is set to a username that doesn’t exist, retrieval will never create the topic/embed, so the iframe will keep showing “Loading…” indefinitely, with no indication why.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:16 — post.user.small_avatar_url/username with no nil guard (deleted user raises); blank SiteSetting.logo_url renders an empty-src img (lines 8, 26).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9 — the task promises URL *validation*, but embed_url gets only a presence check: no scheme, no allowlist, no normalization, no length cap. ensure_embeddable validates the *referer*, an unrelated value — a permitted referer can request retrieval of an arbitrary embed_url.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 / embed_controller.rb:26 — exact case-sensitive `!=` host comparison; `WWW.Example.com`, apex vs www, and port-bearing hosts all fail. This is the only validation the feature has.

However, the finding claims case-sensitivity and port-bearing hosts will fail: Ruby’s `URI(...).host` is normalized to lowercase, and it does not include the port (so a referer like `http://example.com:3000` still yields host `example.com`). adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — `force: true` retrofitted into an ALREADY-SHIPPED migration, i.e. a DROP TABLE added to a migration that has run on production. Unrelated to embeds.

While this won’t affect databases where the migration has already been applied (it won’t re-run), it can cause unintended data loss if the migration is re-run (e.g., on rollback/re-migrate, or in environments where the table exists but the migration isn't marked as run).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` dropped, so imported topics get the import timestamp instead of their real date, while replies still preserve theirs. Also converts an offline XML transform into a live HTTP fetch per thread with no rescue — one dead permalink aborts the run — and on re-run returns the pre-existing post so comments are re-imported as duplicates.

The claim that re-runs will duplicate comments is not fully verifiable from this diff alone because the reply-import de-duplication logic is not shown, though it is plausible since `TopicEmbed.import` will return an existing post for the same `embed_url` and the Thor task still iterates `t[:posts]` afterward.
